title: LIHEAP energy bill assistance opens for eligible Illinois families

LIHEAP energy bill assistance opens for eligible Illinois families
Illinois families meeting certain criteria can now apply for energy bill assistance through LIHEAP. Priority is given to seniors, people with disabilities, families with young children, and those facing utility disconnection. Applications are available online via the Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity.
The Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program began accepting applications on Oct. 1 from eligible Illinois households to help pay for home energy services, including heating gas, propane, and electricity.
According to the announcement, priority groups now able to apply include older adults aged 60 or above, people with disabilities, families with young children aged five or younger, and households that are disconnected from their utilities, have received a disconnection notice, or have less than 25% remaining in their propane tank. All other income-eligible households will be able to start applying on Nov. 1.
Applications can be submitted through the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity website. Applicants can also locate their local LIHEAP office through the same site.
Weber, a Republican who was elected to the Illinois State House in 2019 representing the state's 64th House District and replacing previous state representative Barbara Wheeler, has been involved in promoting resources for constituents, according to Representative Weber's office.
The program aims to provide support during periods of high energy demand and financial need.
